record.question: Grapefruit juice can cause drug–food interactions mainly by:
options: Enhancing digestion by increasing the bioavailability
Inhibiting CYP3A4 enzymes and increasing drug levels
Preventing drug absorption by increasing plasma protein binding
Increasing stomach acid by increasing the action of proton pumps
record.explanation: Answer B: Inhibiting CYP3A4 enzymes and increasing drug levels. Grapefruit can inhibit intestinal CYP3A4 and increase exposure to certain susceptible drugs, creating clinically important interactions. Source/context note: Interaction applies only to particular drugs and may involve transporters as well as CYP3A4. Reference: https://www.fda.gov/consumers/consumer-updates/grapefruit-juice-and-some-drugs-dont-mix. Verified worked solution, unofficial. Original printed wording and option order reviewed; no matching examiner key is asserted.
